scenes.heading: Concurrency, Scaling & Resource Isolation
scenes.narration: As users multiply, warehouses must serve many queries at once without letting workloads interfere with each other.

scenes.heading: The concurrency challenge
bullets: A single warehouse has finite compute, so queries eventually queue.
One giant query can hog resources and stall interactive dashboards.
Mixed workloads, like loads and BI, compete for the same slots.
The fix is isolation plus elastic scaling for bursts of demand.
scenes.narration: Every compute cluster has a ceiling, so beyond a point new queries wait in a queue. A single heavy job can monopolize resources and make dashboards feel sluggish. The solution is to isolate different workloads and scale out automatically when concurrency spikes.

scenes.heading: Isolating workloads
scenes.narration: A common pattern is to give each team or workload its own virtual warehouse over shared storage. Heavy ETL runs on one warehouse while interactive BI runs on another, so they never contend. Each warehouse can then scale out on its own when its particular demand rises.

scenes.heading: Snowflake vs Redshift concurrency
scenes.narration: Snowflake handles concurrency by adding extra clusters to a warehouse when queries start queuing. Redshift instead spins up transient concurrency-scaling clusters to absorb bursts of read queries. Both approaches keep latency stable under load, differing mainly in how they provision the extra capacity.

scenes.text: Isolate workloads onto dedicated compute and scale out on concurrency so no query ever starves another.
scenes.narration: Give each workload its own compute and let it scale out under load, and every user gets consistent performance.
